allclose.describe: a, b = ones vectors, shape (1000*s,), equal-shape broadcast
allclose.formula: 7*numel(broadcast(a,b)) - 1 (min 1): 6 FLOPs/elem tolerance core (sub + 2*abs + mul + add + cmp) + (numel-1) all-reduce
allclose.notes: Data-independent; cost on the broadcast shape of a and b. complex_factor 2.0 applies only to complex inputs.

append.describe: arr = ones(1000*s), values = ones(100), flattened append (axis=None)
append.notes: Cost is sum of input sizes regardless of axis; values kept fixed at 100 so scaling tests the arr term.

apply_along_axis.describe: a = ones((1000*s, 4)), func1d=np.sum along axis 1 -> output shape (1000*s,)
apply_along_axis.formula: numel(output); inner func1d's own fnp ops are billed separately (local callback)
apply_along_axis.notes: func1d here is plain numpy on base ndarrays (uncounted), so measured = wrapper cost only; an fnp func1d would add its own deducts. Emits a local-callback warning.

apply_over_axes.describe: a = ones((1000*s, 4)), func=np.sum over axis 1 -> output shape (1000*s, 1)
apply_over_axes.formula: numel(output); output keeps dims (reduced axes -> length 1), so = numel(input)/prod(reduced axis lengths). Inner func's fnp ops billed separately
apply_over_axes.notes: Reduces over the fixed axis (length 4) so cost scales with s; func is plain numpy (uncounted). Emits a local-callback warning.

arange.notes: Cost set via deduct_after from the actual result size; billing dtype = dtype kwarg (else result_type of args).

argpartition.describe: a = seeded rng.random(1000*s), single kth=500, default axis=-1
argpartition.formula: num_slices * n * len(kth), n = shape[axis], num_slices = numel/n (1 for 0-d; min 1)
argpartition.notes: Linear quickselect per kth; data-independent. kth=500 stays valid for all s>=1.

argsort.describe: a = seeded rng.random(1000*s), 1-D indirect sort along default axis=-1
argsort.formula: num_slices * n*ceil(log2(n)), n = shape[axis] (n = numel for axis=None), num_slices = numel/n; min 1

argwhere.notes: Charged on input size (one predicate test per element), not on the number of nonzeros found; weight matches nonzero.

array.describe: x = ones(1000*s) ndarray copied via fnp.array
array.notes: Ingestion copy billed at 1 FLOP/element; billing dtype = dtype kwarg if given, else input dtype.

array_equal.describe: a, b = identical ones vectors, shape (1000*s,)
array_equal.formula: max(numel(a), numel(b)) (min 1); no broadcasting (shape mismatch just returns False)
array_equal.notes: One comparison per element of the larger operand; registry note says numel(a) but code takes max of both sizes.

array_equiv.describe: a, b = identical ones vectors, shape (1000*s,), trivial broadcast
array_equiv.formula: numel(broadcast(a,b)) (min 1); falls back to max(numel(a), numel(b)) when shapes do not broadcast
array_equiv.notes: Broadcasting equality check; cost on the broadcast shape, one comparison per element.

as_symmetric.describe: all-ones (64s, 64s) matrix tagged with symmetry=(0,1) (k=1 generator)
as_symmetric.formula: k*(7*n - 1), n = numel(data), k = #non-identity generators of the symmetry group (one allclose(data, permuted) per generator); floor 1. Canonical pair-swap symmetry=(0,1) has k=1 -> 7*n - 1
as_symmetric.notes: flopscope-module op (flops.as_symmetric, not fnp); cost scales with generator count k, canonical input pins k=1; matrix must be square so s scales both dims (quadratic law verified at s=1,2)

asarray_chkfinite.formula: numel(output) (one finiteness check per element; scalar input costs 1)
asarray_chkfinite.notes: cost set post-call via set_cost(result.size); complex_factor 2.0 applies at billing only

bartlett.formula: 4*n, n = window length M (compare + divide + add + select per sample); floor 1
bartlett.notes: int-parameter op, dt unused; always bills float64 dtype internally (numpy windows return float64)

bincount.formula: numel(x) (one bucket increment per element); floor 1
bincount.notes: integer-only op (float/complex dtypes raise, matching numpy; registry complex_factor='illegal'); cost ignores optional weights= kwarg

bitwise_and.notes: Integer/bool only (numpy raises TypeError on float/complex, so float32/float64/complex128 billed columns correctly record raises); 1 FLOP per broadcast output element via _counted_binary.

bitwise_count.notes: Popcount, requires numpy>=2.1 (present: 2.2.6); integer-only; billed 1 FLOP/element via _counted_unary regardless of operand bit width.

bitwise_invert.notes: Same numpy ufunc as invert/bitwise_not (numpy 2.0 array-API alias); integer/bool only; 1 FLOP/element via _counted_unary.

bitwise_left_shift.notes: Cost independent of shift amount; integer-only (floats/complex raise); 1 FLOP per broadcast output element via _counted_binary.

bitwise_not.notes: Alias of invert (same numpy ufunc); integer/bool only; 1 FLOP/element via _counted_unary.

bitwise_or.notes: Integer/bool only (float/complex raise); 1 FLOP per broadcast output element via _counted_binary.

bitwise_right_shift.notes: Cost independent of shift amount; integer-only (floats/complex raise); 1 FLOP per broadcast output element via _counted_binary.

bitwise_xor.notes: Integer/bool only (float/complex raise); 1 FLOP per broadcast output element via _counted_binary.

blackman.formula: 40*n, n = window length M (2 cosine evals at transcendental rate 16 + 8 arithmetic per sample; the 0.42 term is a constant); floor 1
blackman.notes: int-parameter op, dt unused; always bills float64 dtype internally (numpy windows return float64)

block.notes: cost set post-call via set_cost(result.size); independent of nesting depth, only output size matters

bmat.formula: numel(output) (block assembly, one copy per element; weight matches block)
bmat.notes: returns np.matrix; cost set post-call via set_cost(result.size), structurally identical to block

choose.describe: (1000s,) index array (arange % 3) selecting from 3 choice arrays
choose.formula: numel(output) (one indexed gather per output element)
choose.notes: cost set post-call via set_cost(result.size); independent of the number of choice arrays

clip.formula: max(n_bounds, 1) * numel(output), n_bounds = #non-None bounds (0..2), output = broadcast of a with all bound arrays (symmetry-reduced via pointwise_cost). Canonical 2 scalar bounds -> 2*numel
clip.notes: one compare-select per bound per output elem; no-bound clip (numpy>=2.1) still pays a numel copy floor; integer bounds 0/2 keep all billed dtypes valid

column_stack.formula: sum(numel(input_i)) (= numel(output): one copy per element); floor 1
column_stack.notes: cost computed pre-call from input sizes (max(sum, 1)), which equals numel(output)

compress.describe: (1000s,) bool mask (exactly half true) selecting from (1000s,) ones -> (500s,) output
compress.formula: len(condition) + 4*numel(output) (scan 1 FLOP per condition flag + gather-tier 4 FLOPs per selected element; mirrors extract). Data-dependent via selected count; canonical half-true mask -> n + 4*(n/2) = 3n
compress.notes: registry note 'numel(input)' is stale vs code (charges cond scan + 4x gather per selected elem); cost depends on #selected, exact for the half-true canonical mask

concat.describe: concat of two (1000s,) float32 vectors along axis 0 -> output (2000s,)
concat.notes: NumPy 2.x alias of concatenate; cost billed from result.size (floor 1), one copy per output element.

concatenate.describe: concatenate of two (1000s,) float32 vectors along axis 0 -> output (2000s,)
concatenate.notes: Cost computed as max(sum of input sizes, 1), which equals numel(output); same model as concat.

convolve.describe: convolve of (1000s,) with (64,) float32 kernels, mode='full' (default)
convolve.formula: mode-dependent, n=numel(a), m=numel(v): full (default) max(2*n*m - n - m, 1); valid (2*min(n,m)-1)*(max(n,m)-min(n,m)+1); same = exact per-output-position dot-length sum (numpy C layout)
convolve.notes: FMA=2 dots; full deliberately keeps legacy 2nm-n-m (no +1) unlike correlate full which uses 2nm-n-m+1.

copyto.describe: copyto of a float64 (1000s,) source into a float32 (1000s,) dst -- lossy narrowing cast, the charged branch
copyto.formula: 0 for a lossless copy (can_cast safe, e.g. same dtype or widening); numel(dst) for a value-changing cast; count_nonzero(where) when a where mask is given
copyto.notes: Canonical input must be a lossy cast (src float64 -> dst dt=float32) to exercise the charged branch; a same-dtype copy bills 0. Mirrors astype.

corrcoef.describe: corrcoef of an (8, 1000s) float32 matrix: f=8 variables, n=1000s samples (random data so variances are nonzero)
corrcoef.formula: 2*f^2*n + 2*f*n + 2*f^2 + f  (f = variables = rows of x plus rows of y, n = samples; cov Gram+centering plus f^2 normalizing divides at 2 FLOPs and f sqrts at 1 FLOP)
corrcoef.notes: Bills at float64 regardless of input dtype (numpy computes corrcoef via result_type(x, y, float64)); 1-D x counts as f=1.

correlate.describe: correlate of (1000s,) with (64,) float32 vectors, mode='valid' (default): 1000s-63 dots of length 64
correlate.formula: mode-dependent, n=numel(a), m=numel(v): valid (default) (2*min(n,m)-1)*(max(n,m)-min(n,m)+1); full max(2*n*m - n - m + 1, 1); same = exact per-output-position dot-length sum (numpy C layout)
correlate.notes: FMA=2 dot per output position; shares _correlate_cost with convolve but full mode here includes the +1 (exact count), unlike convolve full.

cov.describe: cov of an (8, 1000s) float32 matrix: f=8 variables, n=1000s samples
cov.formula: 2*f^2*n + 2*f*n  (f = variables = rows of m plus rows of y, n = samples; f^2 length-n Gram dots at FMA=2 plus a 2-FLOP-per-element centering pass)
cov.notes: Bills at float64 regardless of input dtype (numpy computes cov via result_type(m, y, float64)); 1-D input counts as f=1.

cross.describe: cross of two (1000s, 3) float32 stacks of 3-vectors -> output (1000s, 3), 9 FLOPs per vector pair
cross.formula: max(3*numel(output), 1)  (2 mul + 1 sub per output scalar, non-FMA)
cross.notes: Billed from the ACTUAL result size so axisa/axisb/axisc, broadcasting, and the 2-D z-only path are exact; complex factor 4.7.

delete.describe: delete index 0 from a (1000s,) float32 vector -> output (1000s - 1,)
delete.notes: Cost billed from result.size after the call, so any obj form (index, slice, mask) is exact.

diag.describe: diag extract of the main diagonal of a (64s, 64s) float32 matrix -> 64s elements copied
diag.notes: Canonical input measures the 2-D extract branch (min(m,n)); the 1-D construct branch bills the full (n+|k|)^2 output matrix (see diagflat).

diagflat.describe: diagflat of a (64s,) float32 vector -> full (64s, 64s) output matrix materialised
diagflat.notes: Cost billed from result.size, so quadratic in numel(v); k offset enlarges the output accordingly.

diagonal.notes: Returns a read-only view; code deducts flop_cost=0 (src/flopscope/_array_ops.py:1290). Registry note 'Cost: numel(input)' is stale vs code.

diff.formula: B*(n*L - n*(n+1)/2) where L = diff-axis length (incl. prepend/append elements), B = prod of other dims; default n=1 gives numel(output)
diff.notes: Closed form sums the n subtract passes (numpy iterates a = a[1:]-a[:-1]); canonical input uses default n=1, no prepend/append.

digitize.notes: Bins fixed at 16 (ceil(log2)=4) so scaling tests the n dimension; cost is data-independent. Complex dtypes are rejected (complex_factor 'illegal').

dot.formula: M*N*(2K-1) for 2-D matmul (einsum-routed 'ij,jk->ik'); general case bills the einsum accumulation cost of the equivalent contraction subscripts
dot.notes: Registry note 'cost = M*K*N' is stale: dot routes through the (2K-1)*M einsum engine (src/flopscope/_pointwise.py:2482); 1-D/ND cases map to i,i-> and outer-contract subscripts.

dstack.notes: Cost set post-call from result.size (deduct_after); 1-D inputs are atleast_3d-promoted so output numel = 2*n.

ediff1d.notes: to_begin/to_end extras add their numel to the charge but never change billing dtype; canonical input omits them.

einsum_path.formula: 1 (flat charge; path optimization itself is uncounted and no numeric output is produced)
einsum_path.notes: Constant 1-FLOP charge regardless of operand sizes (src/flopscope/_einsum.py:670); input scales harmlessly, cost does not.

extract.notes: Bills a full input scan; independent of condition density and output size.

fft.fft.describe: 1-D np.ones array of length 1024*s, dtype dt; full-length transform (n=None, axis=-1)
fft.fft.formula: B * 5*n*ceil(log2(n)) where n = transform length (a.shape[axis] or explicit n), B = numel/a.shape[axis] batch count; 0 if n <= 1
fft.fft.notes: Code: _batch_count_1d(a,axis)*fft_cost(n), fft_cost=5*n*ceil(log2(n)). complex_factor=1.0 (complex real-FLOPs priced into the 5x constant), so complex64 input bills the same. Verified exact at s=1 (51200) and s=2 (112640).

fft.fft2.describe: 2-D np.ones array of shape (64*s, 64), dtype dt; both axes transformed (s=None, axes=(-2,-1))
fft.fft2.formula: B * 5*N*(ceil(log2(d1))+ceil(log2(d2))) where (d1,d2) = transform shape (s= param, default input shape on axes), N = d1*d2, B = batch count over non-transform axes; dims <= 1 contribute 0 to the log sum
fft.fft2.notes: Code is fftn_cost = 5*N*SUM of per-axis ceil(log2(d_i)) — NOT the registry note's 5*N*ceil(log2(N)) (stale wording; equal only for power-of-two dims). Verified exact at s=1/s=2 (245760/532480).

fft.fftfreq.describe: scalar grid length n = 1024*s (no array input; dt unused — op takes no dtype and always produces a float64 grid)
fft.fftfreq.formula: max(n, 1) — n FLOPs, one multiply per frequency-grid element (index grid scaled by 1/(n*d))
fft.fftfreq.notes: Op has no array/dtype parameter; deduct hardcodes billing dtype float64 (raw_dtype set to match). Cost is exactly n for n>=1 (max(n,1) floor). Verified exact at s=1/s=2 (1024/2048).

fft.fftn.describe: 3-D np.ones array of shape (8, 16, 64*s), dtype dt; all three axes transformed (s=None, axes=None)
fft.fftn.formula: B * 5*N*sum_i(ceil(log2(d_i))) over transform dims d_i (s= param, default full input shape or shape on given axes), N = prod(d_i), B = batch count over non-transform axes; dims <= 1 contribute 0
fft.fftn.notes: 3-D input exercises the per-axis log SUM (3+4+ceil(log2(64*s))); registry note's 5*N*ceil(log2(N)) is stale wording vs code. Verified exact at s=1/s=2 (532480/1146880).

fft.hfft.describe: 1-D np.ones half-spectrum of length 512*s+1, dtype dt, giving default real output length n_out = 2*(m-1) = 1024*s
fft.hfft.formula: B * 5*(n_out//2)*ceil(log2(n_out)) where n_out = explicit n or 2*(m-1) for input axis length m, B = numel/m batch count; 0 if n_out <= 1
fft.hfft.notes: Code: batch * hfft_cost(n_out); hfft is a c2r transform (irfft of conj) so cost keys on the OUTPUT length. Input length chosen 512*s+1 so n_out = 1024*s exactly. Verified exact at s=1/s=2 (25600/56320).

fft.ifft.describe: 1-D np.ones array of length 1024*s, dtype dt; full-length inverse transform (n=None, axis=-1)
fft.ifft.formula: B * 5*n*ceil(log2(n)) where n = transform length (a.shape[axis] or explicit n), B = numel/a.shape[axis] batch count; 0 if n <= 1 (1/n normalization not billed separately)
fft.ifft.notes: Identical cost path to fft.fft (batch * fft_cost(n)); numpy accepts real input (treated as zero-imag spectrum). Verified exact at s=1/s=2 (51200/112640).

fft.ifft2.describe: 2-D np.ones array of shape (64*s, 64), dtype dt; both axes transformed (s=None, axes=(-2,-1))
fft.ifft2.formula: B * 5*N*(ceil(log2(d1))+ceil(log2(d2))) where (d1,d2) = transform shape (s= param, default input shape on axes), N = d1*d2, B = batch count; dims <= 1 contribute 0 (normalization not billed separately)
fft.ifft2.notes: Identical cost path to fft.fft2 (batch * fftn_cost with per-axis log sum). Verified exact at s=1/s=2 (245760/532480).

fft.ifftn.describe: 3-D np.ones array of shape (8, 16, 64*s), dtype dt; all three axes transformed (s=None, axes=None)
fft.ifftn.formula: B * 5*N*sum_i(ceil(log2(d_i))) over transform dims d_i (s= param, default full input shape or shape on given axes), N = prod(d_i), B = batch count; dims <= 1 contribute 0 (normalization not billed separately)
fft.ifftn.notes: Identical cost path to fft.fftn (batch * fftn_cost, per-axis log sum). Verified exact at s=1/s=2 (532480/1146880).

fft.ihfft.describe: 1-D real np.ones signal of length 1024*s, dtype dt (natural real-input domain of ihfft)
fft.ihfft.formula: B * 5*(n//2)*ceil(log2(n)) where n = input axis length (or explicit n), B = numel/a.shape[axis] batch count; 0 if n <= 1
fft.ihfft.notes: Code: batch * hfft_cost(n) with n = input length (numpy computes conj(rfft(a,n))); half-spectrum symmetry gives the n//2 factor. Verified exact at s=1/s=2 (25600/56320).

fft.irfft.describe: 1-D np.ones half-spectrum of length 512*s+1, dtype dt, giving default real output length n = 2*(m-1) = 1024*s
fft.irfft.formula: B * 5*(n//2)*ceil(log2(n)) where n = real output length (explicit n or 2*(m-1) for input axis length m), B = numel/m batch count; 0 if n <= 1
fft.irfft.notes: Code: batch * rfft_cost(n) with n keyed on the OUTPUT length (c2r symmetry halves the work). Input length 512*s+1 makes n = 1024*s exactly; numpy accepts a real half-spectrum (zero imag). Verified exact at s=1/s=2 (25600/56320).

fft.irfft2.describe: 2-D np.ones half-spectrum of shape (64*s, 33), dtype dt, giving default real output transform shape (64*s, 2*(33-1)) = (64*s, 64)
fft.irfft2.formula: B * 5*(N//2)*(ceil(log2(d1))+ceil(log2(d2))) where transform shape defaults to (a.shape[axes[0]], 2*(a.shape[axes[1]]-1)) (or explicit s=), N = d1*d2, B = batch count over non-transform axes; dims <= 1 contribute 0
fft.irfft2.notes: Code: batch * rfftn_cost(s_for_cost) — last transform axis expands to 2*(d-1) for the cost shape, then 5*(N//2)*per-axis log SUM (registry's ceil(log2(N)) is stale wording). Verified exact at s=1/s=2 (122880/266240).

fft.irfftn.describe: 3-D half-spectrum array (8, 16, 4*s+1), all axes transformed (B=1); output transform shape (8, 16, 8*s), N=1024*s
fft.irfftn.formula: B * 5*(N//2)*sum_i ceil(log2(d_i)) over the OUTPUT transform shape: d_last = 2*(a.shape[last transform axis]-1) unless s= given, other d_i = input dims; N = prod(d_i), axes with d_i<=1 contribute 0 to the log sum; B = batch count over non-transform axes; 0 if N<=1
fft.irfftn.notes: Cost billed on output shape (last axis 2*(m-1)); real float32 input is valid (numpy promotes to complex). Registry note says ceil(log2(N)) but code sums per-axis ceils (rfftn_cost) — equal only for power-of-2 dims; formula follows code.

fft.rfft.formula: B * 5*(n//2)*ceil(log2(n)) — n = transform length (a.shape[axis] unless n= given), B = a.size/a.shape[axis] batched 1-D transforms; 0 if n<=1
fft.rfft.notes: Half of the complex-FFT cost via n//2 (conjugate symmetry); the 5x radix-2 constant already prices complex real-FLOPs. Cost depends only on n and batch shape, not values.

fft.rfft2.describe: 2-D array (64*s, 64) (np.ones), default axes (-2,-1) so B=1, N=4096*s
fft.rfft2.formula: B * 5*(N//2)*(ceil(log2(d1)) + ceil(log2(d2))) — (d1,d2) = transform shape over the two axes (s= or their dims), N = d1*d2, dims <=1 contribute 0 to the log sum; B = batch count over non-transform axes; 0 if N<=1
fft.rfft2.notes: Registry note says ceil(log2(N)) but code (rfftn_cost) sums per-axis ceil(log2(d_i)) — equal only when dims are powers of 2; formula follows code.

fft.rfftfreq.describe: scalar n=1024*s, default d=1.0; no array input (dt unused)
fft.rfftfreq.formula: n//2 + 1 (min 1) — one multiply per returned frequency: integer index grid 0..n//2 scaled by 1/(n*d)
fft.rfftfreq.notes: No array input so dt is ignored; deduct always declares float64 (the output grid dtype), so all billed-dtype columns coincide.

fft.rfftn.formula: B * 5*(N//2)*sum_i ceil(log2(d_i)) — d_i = transform shape over the chosen axes (default all axes; s= overrides), N = prod(d_i), dims <=1 contribute 0 to the log sum; B = batch count over non-transform axes; 0 if N<=1
fft.rfftn.notes: Registry note says ceil(log2(N)) but code (rfftn_cost) sums per-axis ceil(log2(d_i)) — equal only for power-of-2 dims; formula follows code. 3-D input exercises the true N-D path (distinct from rfft2).

fill_diagonal.formula: min(m, n) for ndim>=2 (diagonal length; numel(a) fallback for ndim<2, though numpy itself rejects 1-D)
fill_diagonal.notes: In-place mutation, returns None; square input so min(m,n) scales with s. wrap kwarg does not change the charge.

flatnonzero.notes: Full-scan charge, independent of how many elements are nonzero.

fromfunction.describe: fromfunction(lambda i: i, (1000,), dtype=dt) — identity over a 1-D coordinate grid
fromfunction.notes: Cost = result.size (1 if the callback returns a sizeless object); the user callback itself runs uncounted on base numpy index arrays (local_callback op, emits a remote-callback warning).

fromiter.describe: fromiter over a prebuilt 1000-element python list with count=n
fromiter.notes: Iterator materialisation billed at numel(output), weight 1.0 (matches array/concatenate); registry docstring tier says 'free' but the live binding deducts numel. Input uses a list (re-iterable) so the callable is safe to invoke more than once.

full.notes: Raw flop_cost = numel(output); production weight is 0.0 (constant-fill free tier), so billed cost is 0 under shipped weights — raw sheet measures the unit-weight numel.

full_like.describe: full_like(a, 3) on a prebuilt 1-D array of 1000 elements
full_like.notes: Cost keyed on the INPUT array's size (equals output numel; shape kwarg not consulted for cost); billing dtype = explicit dtype kwarg else a.dtype. Production weight 0.0 (constant-fill free tier).

gcd.notes: Code bills flat 1 FLOP/element (pointwise tier via _counted_binary) although Euclid's gcd is O(log min(a,b)) iterations per element — data-independent billed cost; integer-only.

geomspace.notes: Cost = result.size via deduct_after (= num for scalar start/stop; num*B when array start/stop broadcast), then production weight 16.0 and complex_factor 5.5 apply. Known undercount finding (charges 1 per elem vs ~4 honest) — formula documents the code as-is.

gradient.describe: gradient of a 1-D arange(1000) array, default unit spacing
gradient.formula: sum over axes of 2*S*max(L-2,0)//L with S=numel(f), L=shape[ax] (scalar/no spacing); each coordinate-array axis adds +3*(L-1) if its diffs are uniform, else +3*S*(L-2)//L + 10*(L-2) + 3*(L-1) + 4*S//L; 0-d input costs 1
gradient.notes: 1-D no-varargs canonical input hits only the base term: 2*S*(S-2)//S = 2*(n-2); coordinate-array spacing surcharges are exercised only when 1-D coord arrays are passed. Billing dtype = f.dtype only (spacing args never change output dtype).

hamming.describe: hamming(1000) — window length M=1000 (no dtype arg; always float64)
hamming.notes: Code bills 2 FLOPs/sample (FMA=2: 1 mul + 1 add); registry notes line ('cost: n, one cosine') is stale vs hamming_cost(). Op takes no dtype — numpy windows always return and are billed as float64.

hanning.describe: hanning(1000) — window length M=1000 (no dtype arg; always float64)
hanning.notes: Same skeleton as hamming: hanning_cost = max(2n,1), 1 mul + 1 add per sample under FMA=2; registry 'one cosine per sample' note is stale vs code. Always float64-billed.

histogram.describe: histogram of a 1-D arange(1000) array with bins=10 (default int bins)
histogram.formula: max(n*ceil(log2(bins)), 1) for int bins (array edges use bins=len(edges); ceil(log2(.)) floored at 1); string estimators bill max(n*(2 + estimator_cost + ceil(log2(resolved_bins))), 1) via deferred cost
histogram.notes: Canonical input takes the int-bins branch: n*ceil(log2(10)) = 4n. Array bin edges join the billing dtype tuple; 'stone' estimator costs max(100, isqrt(n)) per element.

histogram2d.describe: histogram2d of two 1-D arange(1000) arrays with bins=10
histogram2d.formula: max(n*(ceil(log2(bx)) + ceil(log2(by))), 1) for int / (int,int) / (edges,edges) bins (edges use len(edge array)); any other bins spec bills max(n, 1)
histogram2d.notes: n = x.size; bins=10 gives n*(4+4) = 8n. Array-valued bin edges also join the billing dtype tuple alongside x.dtype and y.dtype.

histogram_bin_edges.describe: histogram_bin_edges of a 1-D arange(1000) array with bins=10
histogram_bin_edges.formula: max(n, 1) for int or explicit-edge bins; string estimators bill max(n*(2 + estimator_cost), 1) with estimator_cost = max(100, isqrt(n)) for 'stone' else a per-estimator constant
histogram_bin_edges.notes: Int-bins branch is a flat n (min/max scan); bin count does not enter the cost — only the string-estimator branch scales beyond n.

histogramdd.formula: n*d*ceil(log2(b)) for int bins b (d = sample dimensionality); n*sum_i(ceil(log2(b_i))) for per-axis bins (b_i = int count or len(edges_i)); n otherwise
histogramdd.notes: Binning as d binary searches per point: ceil(log2(10))=4 so cost=12*n; per-axis edge arrays use len(edges_i) not bin count; non-int/non-sequence bins fall back to n.

hstack.notes: Pure copy cost, one FLOP per output element; registry note matches code (src/flopscope/_array_ops.py:706).

in1d.formula: (n+m)*ceil(log2(n+m)) sort path; max((n+m)*ceil(log2(n+m)), 2*n*m) when numpy's masked-loop path triggers (object dtype, or non-integer dtypes with m < 10*n**0.145)
in1d.notes: Canonical float32 m=1000 >= 10*n**0.145 (~27) so sort path applies; numpy<2.4 only (raises UnsupportedFunctionError on >=2.4); branch logic in _membership_cost (src/flopscope/_sorting_ops.py:485).

indices.formula: numel of materialized output: len(dims)*prod(dims) dense; sum(dims) when sparse=True
indices.notes: No array input; dt is passed as the output dtype= (np.indices accepts float dtypes); cost set post-call from result.size (deduct_after, src/flopscope/_array_ops.py:2464).

inner.formula: einsum-routed contraction M*(2*K-1), K = shared last-axis length, M = numel(output): vectors 2*n-1; matrices (a,k)x(b,k) -> a*b*(2*k-1)
inner.notes: Registry note 'cost = N (weight-calibrated)' is stale: op routes through the einsum engine ('i,i->') and bills 2n-1 measured; complex_factor='exact' handled by the contraction family.

insert.notes: Cost set post-call from result.size (deduct_after); rebuild-copy model, one FLOP per output element.

interp.formula: 3*n + n*ceil(log2(len(xp))), n = numel(x) (binary search per query + 3-op blend)
interp.notes: Scales in x only (xp fixed at 1024 so search term is 10n). Billing dtypes force float64 + fp.dtype (np.interp computes in float64), so production dtype rates bill float64 even for float32 inputs; unit-mode raw unaffected.

intersect1d.formula: n*ceil(log2(n)) + m*ceil(log2(m)) + (n+m)*ceil(log2(n+m)) (default: unique() both inputs + concat-sort); (n+m)*ceil(log2(n+m)) when assume_unique=True
intersect1d.notes: Registry note only shows the assume_unique=True branch; code default (assume_unique=False) adds the two per-input unique() sorts (src/flopscope/_sorting_ops.py:599-605); n,m floored at 1.

invert.notes: Bitwise NOT (same numpy ufunc as bitwise_not/bitwise_invert); integer/bool only; 1 FLOP/element via _counted_unary.

is_symmetric.formula: k*(7*numel - 1), k = #non-identity generators (symmetric pair of axes -> k=1; S_j on j axes -> k=j-1)
is_symmetric.notes: Lives at flopscope top level (flops.is_symmetric), not fnp; square constraint means s scales the side so cost is quadratic in s (7*1024*s**2-1); per-generator allclose transpose-compare = 7n-1.

isclose.notes: Binary op (a, b) despite counted_unary registry category — old single-arg default input failed; 6 FLOPs per broadcast output element = sub + 2*abs + mul + add + cmp (dedicated wrapper, _pointwise.py:1366).

isfinite.notes: Simple elementwise test, one FLOP per input element (src/flopscope/_array_ops.py:1522).

isin.formula: (n+m)*ceil(log2(n+m)) sort path; max((n+m)*ceil(log2(n+m)), 2*n*m) when numpy's masked-loop path triggers (object dtype, or non-integer dtypes with m < 10*n**0.145)
isin.notes: fnp.isin binds the counted _sorting_ops version (imported after _array_ops' free passthrough in numpy/__init__.py); same _membership_cost as in1d; canonical float32 m=1000 takes the sort path.

isinf.notes: One inf-classification per input element (src/flopscope/_array_ops.py isinf: flop_cost=x.size); output is bool so cost keys on input numel.

isnan.notes: One NaN-classification per input element (src/flopscope/_array_ops.py isnan: flop_cost=x.size); same skeleton as isinf/isfinite.

ix_.formula: sum(len(a_i)) over the input sequences (= total numel of the returned mesh arrays; a boolean input contributes its nonzero count)
ix_.notes: Each returned open-mesh array has numel = len of its input, so cost = sum of input lengths (src/flopscope/_array_ops.py ix_: sum(a.size for a in result)); int32 because canonical use is integer indices (floats are accepted by np.ix_ itself).

kaiser.formula: 23*M (per sample: 1 Bessel I0 at transcendental tier 16 + 7 arithmetic FLOPs, FMA=2); floor 1
kaiser.notes: No array input so dt is unused; op always returns and bills float64 internally (src/flopscope/_window.py kaiser_cost: max(23*n, 1)).

kron.notes: One multiply per output element (src/flopscope/_pointwise.py kron: max(a.size*b.size, 1)); complex_factor 6.0 applies only on complex dtypes.

lcm.notes: Integer-only ufunc (float/complex input raises TypeError) — prior float32 default input failed; raw cost is one per broadcast output element, the heavier per-element euclid work is carried by the op weight (16.0), not the raw formula.

ldexp.notes: x2 (exponent) must be an integer dtype — the generic float+float input fails with TypeError; x1 honors dt, x2 is structurally int32.

left_shift.notes: Integer-only ufunc (float input raises TypeError), hence int32 raw dtype; one FLOP per broadcast output element via _counted_binary.

lexsort.formula: k * num_slices * n*ceil(log2(n)) where k = len(keys), n = keys[0].shape[axis], num_slices = keys[0].size // n; floor 1
lexsort.notes: One comparison-sort pass per key per slice at sort_cost(n)=n*ceil(log2 n) (src/flopscope/_sorting_ops.py lexsort); ceil(log2) steps 10->11 across s=1->2 so scaling is n*log n, not linear.

linalg.cond.formula: p in {None,2,-2}: values-only SVD + 1 divide = 2*a*b**2 + 2*b**3 + 1 with a=max(m,n), b=min(m,n) (square: 4*n**3 + 1); other p (square only): 2*k**3 + 4*m*n + 1 with k=min(m,n); x batch
linalg.cond.notes: Canonical input exercises the default p=None (SVD) branch; PSD input keeps cond finite (= n+1). Cost is shape-only either branch.

linalg.cross.formula: 3 * numel(broadcast(x1, x2)) = 9 per output 3-vector (6 mul + 3 sub); last axis must be 3
linalg.cross.notes: Registry note says 'delegates to fnp.cross' but the code bills directly under linalg.cross: out_size*3 where out_size = broadcast INPUT numel (== output numel since last axis is 3).

linalg.det.formula: 2*n**3 // 3 + n per matrix (LU + product of diagonal), x batch
linalg.det.notes: np.linalg.det emits harmless FP-status RuntimeWarnings on this platform for ANY input (even identity, any dtype) - LAPACK kernel status leakage, not input-dependent; input chosen so det value stays finite.

linalg.eig.formula: 25*n**3 per matrix (Hessenberg + Francis QR with eigenvector backtransform), x batch
linalg.eig.notes: Cost is shape-only; symmetric input keeps eigenvalues real (no complex output).

linalg.eigh.formula: 9*n**3 per matrix (tridiagonalization + symmetric QR with vectors), x batch
linalg.eigh.notes: UPLO default 'L'; cost independent of UPLO.

linalg.eigvals.formula: 10*n**3 per matrix (nonsymmetric Hessenberg + QR, values only), x batch
linalg.eigvals.notes: Intentionally costs MORE than eigh (9n^3): nonsymmetric values-only vs symmetric with vectors (comment in eigvals_cost).

linalg.eigvalsh.formula: 4*n**3 // 3 per matrix (tridiagonalization, values only), x batch
linalg.eigvalsh.notes: Code computes max(4*n**3 // 3, 1) (floor division on the full product).

linalg.inv.formula: 2*n**3 per matrix (getrf 2n^3/3 + getri 4n^3/3); n**3//3 + n**3 for SymmetricTensor input; x batch
linalg.inv.notes: Canonical input is a plain (non-SymmetricTensor) array so the general 2n^3 branch is billed; PSD construction guarantees invertibility.

linalg.lstsq.formula: svd(m,n; with U/V) + U^T*b + divide + reconstruct: (6*a*b**2 + 20*b**3) + (2*k*m*c - k*c) + k*c + (2*n*k*c - n*c), a=max(m,n), b=k=min(m,n), c=RHS cols (1 for 1-D b); x batch
linalg.lstsq.notes: Composed from svd_cost(with_vectors=True) + matmul_cost(k,m,c) + k*c + matmul_cost(n,k,c) where matmul_cost(m,k,n) = 2mkn - mn (einsum engine); scales in m only (simplifies to 397312*s + 657376).

linalg.matmul.formula: delegates to top-level matmul: einsum '...ij,...jk->...ik' cost = 2*m*k*n - m*n per 2-D product (x batch for stacked inputs)
linalg.matmul.notes: Pure delegation (no own deduct): the first/only deduct is recorded under op 'matmul', not 'linalg.matmul' - cost-site attribution lands on the top-level op. Sheet note 'm*k*n (weight-calibrated)' is stale; engine bills 2mkn - mn.

linalg.matrix_norm.formula: ord in {'fro',1,-1,inf,-inf} (default 'fro'): 2*m*n; ord in {2,-2,'nuc'}: 2*a*b^2 + 2*b^3 (values-only SVD, a=max(m,n), b=min(m,n)); x batch (product of dims except last two)
linalg.matrix_norm.notes: Default ord='fro' measured: one 2*numel elementwise pass; SVD ords switch to 2ab^2+2b^3.

linalg.matrix_power.formula: (floor(log2(k)) + popcount(k) - 1) * (2*n^3 - n^2) for exponent k>=2 (repeated squaring); 0 for k in {0,1}; k<0 adds one extra (2*n^3 - n^2) for the initial inverse; x batch
linalg.matrix_power.notes: Canonical exponent k=3 -> floor(log2 3)+popcount(3)-1 = 2 matmuls, each matmul_cost(n,n,n)=2n^3-n^2.

linalg.matrix_rank.formula: 2*a*b^2 + 2*b^3 + b, a=max(m,n), b=min(m,n) (values-only SVD + b threshold compares); x batch; 0-D/1-D input: numel
linalg.matrix_rank.notes: SVD term is values-only (2ab^2+2b^3); the +b is min(m,n) singular-value threshold compares.

linalg.multi_dot.formula: optimal matrix-chain multiplication cost (DP over parenthesizations); each binary step (m,k)@(k,n) costs 2*m*k*n - m*n; end vectors promoted to 1-row/1-col matrices
linalg.multi_dot.notes: 3-matrix chain exercises the DP: (B C)-first is optimal for s>=2, both orders tie at s=1; cost is data-independent.

linalg.norm.formula: standard ords (None/'fro'/0/1/-1/2/inf/-inf on vectors; None/'fro'/1/-1/inf/-inf on matrices): 2*numel; general-p vector ord: 18*numel + 16; matrix ord in {2,-2,'nuc'}: 2*a*b^2 + 2*b^3 (values-only SVD, a=max(m,n), b=min(m,n)); x groups (product of non-reduced dims; axis=None -> 1 group)
linalg.norm.notes: Default ord=None on a 1-D vector: 2*numel (FMA=2 multiply+accumulate per element).

linalg.outer.formula: m*n (delegates to fnp.outer: einsum 'i,j->ij', no contracted index so (2K-1)*M with K=1 = one multiply per output element)
linalg.outer.notes: Pure delegation: the deduct (and cost site) is the top-level 'outer' op in _pointwise.py; np.linalg.outer requires 1-D inputs.

linalg.pinv.formula: (6*a*b^2 + 20*b^3) + b + n*b + (2*n*b*m - n*m), a=max(m,n), b=min(m,n) (thin-U/V SVD + threshold + diagonal scale + reconstruction matmul(n,b,m)); x batch
linalg.pinv.notes: SVD term is thin U/V (6ab^2+20b^3, full_matrices=False); pinv is well-defined on the singular all-ones input.

linalg.qr.notes: Default mode='reduced' doubles the Householder factorization count (explicit Q formation); code uses integer (2*k^3)//3.

linalg.slogdet.formula: 2*n^3//3 + 18*n (LU factorization + sum of log|diag|: abs + 16-FLOP log per element + reduce); x batch
linalg.slogdet.notes: PSD input (n*ones + n*I, same recipe as the cholesky canonical) keeps the log-determinant finite; cost is value-independent.

linalg.solve.formula: 2*n^3//3 + 2*n^2*nrhs (LU getrf + two triangular solves getrs); nrhs = b.shape[-1] if b.ndim>=2 else 1; x batch
linalg.solve.notes: A must be nonsingular (all-ones raises LinAlgError) so the PSD recipe n*ones+n*I is used; 1-D b gives nrhs=1.

linalg.svdvals.formula: 2*a*b^2 + 2*b^3 per matrix, a=max(m,n), b=min(m,n), x batch (values-only SVD); top-k (1<=k<b) bills min(4*m*n*k, that)
linalg.svdvals.notes: Delegates to svd_cost(m,n,k,with_vectors=False) in _flops.py; k=None bills economy values-only cost; k<1 raises.

linalg.tensordot.formula: (2*K - 1) * M, K = product of contracted dims, M = numel(output) (einsum accumulation engine; rank>52 falls back to a.size*b.size/K)
linalg.tensordot.notes: Alias: delegates to fnp.tensordot, so the deduct/cost-site op name is 'tensordot' (linalg.tensordot itself never charges); symmetric operands scale cost by unique-element fraction.

linalg.tensorinv.formula: 2*n^3, n = prod(a.shape[:ind]) (reshape then matrix inverse; delegates to inv_cost)
linalg.tensorinv.notes: Input must be square after reshape (prod(shape[:ind])==prod(shape[ind:])); diagonally-dominant seeded matrix guarantees invertibility.

linalg.tensorsolve.input_code:
def make(dt, s=1):
    n = 24 * s
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    mat = np.eye(n, dtype=dt) * n + rng.random((n, n)).astype(dt)
    a = fnp.asarray(mat.reshape(4, 6 * s, 24 * s))
    b = fnp.asarray(np.ones((4, 6 * s), dtype=dt))
    return lambda: fnp.linalg.tensorsolve(a, b)
linalg.tensorsolve.formula: floor(2*n^3/3) + 2*n^2, n = prod(a.shape[2:]) (reshape then solve_cost(n, nrhs=1))
linalg.tensorsolve.notes: Cost model uses fixed ind=2 (wrapper calls tensorsolve_cost(a.shape) without the axes arg), so n = prod of dims from index 2 on regardless of the axes= parameter.

linalg.trace.formula: min(m,n) x batch (diagonal-sum length, offset-adjusted: offset shortens the diagonal)
linalg.trace.notes: Square input so the diagonal length (= the cost) scales with s; an explicit dtype= accumulator joins the billing-dtype tuple.

linalg.vecdot.formula: 2*n - 1 per output element (einsum '...n,...n->...' accumulation), x batch groups
linalg.vecdot.notes: Alias: delegates to fnp.vecdot so the deduct op name is 'vecdot'; sized 500*s because numpy 2.2's float32 vecdot SIMD kernel emits spurious FP-status RuntimeWarnings for n>~1500 (result unaffected); requires numpy>=2.1.

linalg.vector_norm.formula: 2*numel per group for ord in {None,0,1,2,inf,-inf} (default ord=2); general-p costs 18*numel + 16 per group; x batch groups (axis=None -> 1 group)
linalg.vector_norm.notes: numel is the effective shape along the reduced axes; canonical input measures the standard-norm 2*numel branch (general-p branch is 18*numel+16).

linspace.formula: 2*numel(output) (start + i*step per element, FMA=2; broadcast dims from array start/stop are included; with retstep=True bills the samples array only)
linspace.notes: Cost set from the actual result size (src/flopscope/_array_ops.py linspace: 2*samples.size), so array start/stop broadcast B multiplies the bill; scalar endpoints give exactly 2*num.

logspace.formula: numel(output) raw flop_cost (broadcast dims from array start/stop included); the per-element pow/exp price is carried by the production weight (16.0), not the raw count
logspace.notes: Raw cost = result.size (src/flopscope/_counting_ops.py logspace: _op.set_cost(result.size)); production billing multiplies by weight 16.0 and complex_factor 5.5 on complex dtypes.

mask_indices.formula: 2*n^2 + 8*k where n is the matrix dimension and k = numel of each returned index array (2*n^2 boolean-mask scan + 8 per selected pair at gather tier); for np.triu at offset 0, k = n*(n+1)/2
mask_indices.notes: k is data-dependent on mask_func; exact for the canonical triu mask (k=n(n+1)/2 gives 24576*s^2+256*s). No array input so dt is unused; pass RAW np.triu as mask_func (an fnp mask_func would double-bill).

matvec.formula: m*(2n-1) for A (..., m, n) @ v (..., n); batch/broadcast dims multiply the output count M, so cost = M*(2n-1)
matvec.notes: Prior 1-D+1-D input failed (A must be >=2-D); measured 8128 = 64*(2*64-1) confirms the FMA=2 einsum engine — registry note 'output_size * contracted_axis' is stale (would be 8192); spurious FP-status RuntimeWarnings from platform BLAS (same as committed matmul input) are data-independent and harmless. Requires numpy>=2.2.

meshgrid.formula: dense (default): len(xi) * prod(len(x_i)) = total numel of the output grids; sparse=True: sum(len(x_i)); copy=False: 1 (views); floor 1
meshgrid.notes: One copy-FLOP per materialized grid element (src/flopscope/_array_ops.py meshgrid); canonical dense 2-input case bills 2*64s*64.

nanpercentile.formula: num_outputs * axis_dim (= numel(a) for a dense reduce; independent of the number of q values)
nanpercentile.notes: Prior input failed only because q is a required arg; Tier-2 partition model charges one pass over the reduced axis per output and does NOT scale with len(q); cost is shape-based (NaN count irrelevant).

nanquantile.formula: num_outputs * axis_dim (= numel(a) for a dense reduce; independent of the number of q values)
nanquantile.notes: Prior input failed only because q is a required arg; Tier-2 partition model, one pass over the reduced axis per output, no len(q) scaling; complex input is rejected by numpy (registry: illegal).

nanstd.formula: 4*numel + M where M = num_outputs (2 pointwise passes center+square, 2 FMA=2 accumulation passes 2*(numel-M), 2M divides, M sqrts); dense full reduce = 4n+1
nanstd.notes: Shares _variance_family_cost with std/var: 2*numel + 2*(numel-M) + 2M + M = 4*numel + M exactly for dense input; matches committed measurements 4001/8001.

nanvar.formula: 4*numel (2 pointwise passes center+square, 2 FMA=2 accumulation passes 2*(numel-M), 2M divides; the M terms cancel so cost = 4*numel for any axis)
nanvar.notes: Shares _variance_family_cost with var (with_sqrt=False): 2*numel + 2*(numel-M) + 2M = 4*numel exactly for dense input, independent of output count; matches committed measurements 4000/8000.

nonzero.describe: 1-D all-ones float array of 1000*s elements (every element non-zero)
nonzero.notes: Cost = numel(input) regardless of how many elements are non-zero (full scan); verified exact at s=1,2.

outer.describe: outer product of a 64*s-vector with a 64-vector -> (64*s, 64) output
outer.formula: m*n (m = a.size, n = b.size; inputs flattened to 1-D)
outer.notes: Routed through the einsum cost engine ('i,j->ij', K=1 so (2K-1)*M = M = m*n); aliased outer(v, v) takes the symmetric-output path costing n*(n+1)/2. Complex bills exact (complex_factor 6.0 declared).

packbits.describe: 1-D alternating 0/1 int32 array of 1000*s elements packed to bits
packbits.notes: Integer/bool dtypes only (numpy rejects float; complex_factor 'illegal'); each input element is tested+shifted, symmetric with unpackbits which charges numel(output).

pad.describe: 1-D ones array of 1000*s elements padded with linear_ramp, 50*s on each side (compute mode; cost = 2 per padded element)
pad.formula: mode-dependent: 0 for movement modes (constant/edge/empty/wrap/reflect/symmetric with reflect_type='even'); 2*(numel_out - numel_in) for linear_ramp and reflect/symmetric with reflect_type='odd'; per-axis stat cost for maximum/minimum/mean/median: cross_section * min(stat_length, axis_len) per padded side, deduplicated to ONE full-axis stat when both sides use the default full-axis stat_length (+ cross_section divides for mean); mode=<callable> raises
pad.notes: Canonical input measures the linear_ramp compute mode = 2*(numel_out-numel_in) = 200*s; default mode='constant' (and all movement modes) bills 0; pad width scales with s so the measurement exercises the padded-element term, not the free copy of the interior.

partition.describe: 1-D array of 1000*s seeded standard-normal values, single kth=500
partition.formula: numel(a) * len(kth)  (per-slice linear quickselect: num_slices * n * len(kth) with n = shape[axis], num_slices = numel/n)
partition.notes: num_slices*n always equals numel(a), so cost is numel*kth_count for any axis (axis=None is costed as axis=-1, same product); data-independent.

percentile.formula: num_outputs * axis_dim (= numel(a) for a dense reduce; independent of the number of q values)
percentile.notes: Prior input failed only because q is a required arg; Tier-2 partition-based model (_tier2_reduction_cost), one pass over the reduced axis per output element, no len(q) scaling; complex input rejected by numpy (registry: illegal).

piecewise.describe: 1-D arange of 1000*s elements split by two boolean conditions with negate/identity plain-python callbacks
piecewise.notes: local_callback op: emits RemoteCallbackWarning in-process and raises on the remote backend; funclist callbacks run on base ndarrays (their FLOPs are NOT included in the numel(x) charge); condlist must be prebuilt outside the context or its comparison cost leaks in.

place.describe: in-place masked write into a 1000*s ones array, every 2nd element True, 500*s replacement values
place.notes: Charges the full destination size (mask scan), independent of how many mask elements are True; mutates arr in place (zero-copy view).

poly.formula: (3*n^2 + n)//2, n = len(roots) (1-D input); 2-D square-matrix input adds 10*n^3 for companion eigvals
poly.notes: Cost depends only on n = len(roots), data-independent; 2-D branch (+10*n^3 eigvals) not exercised by this input; min-clamped at 1.

polyadd.describe: polyadd of 1000*s-coeff and fixed 100-coeff all-ones polynomials
polyadd.formula: max(n1, n2), n1/n2 = coefficient array lengths
polyadd.notes: Cost is max of the two lengths (only the longer operand scales); data-independent; min-clamped at 1.

polyder.describe: polyder (m=1 default) of a 1000*s-coeff all-ones polynomial
polyder.formula: t*n - t*(t+1)//2, t = min(m, n-1) (n = len(p), m = derivative order; m=1 gives n-1)
polyder.notes: Canonical input uses default m=1 so cost = n-1; one multiply per surviving coefficient per derivative step; min-clamped at 1.

polydiv.describe: polydiv of 1000*s-coeff numerator by fixed 4-coeff divisor (all ones)
polydiv.formula: 1 + Q*(2*n2 + 1), Q = max(n1 - n2 + 1, 0) (per quotient step: 1 scale-divide + n2 mul + n2 sub)
polydiv.notes: Scales with quotient length Q = n1-n2+1; divisor length n2 fixed at 4 so cost = 1 + 9*Q; min-clamped at 1.

polyfit.describe: cubic (deg=3) fit of constant y over 100*s points x in (0, 1]
polyfit.notes: deg fixed at 3 so cost = 32*m; cost ignores rcond/weights (w only joins billing dtypes); min-clamped at 1.

polyint.describe: polyint (m=1 default) of a 1000*s-coeff all-ones polynomial
polyint.formula: m*n + m*(m-1)//2 (n = len(p), m = integration order; m=1 gives n)
polyint.notes: Canonical input uses default m=1 so cost = n; complex k constant would join billing dtypes; min-clamped at 1.

polymul.describe: polymul of 100*s-coeff and fixed 100-coeff all-ones polynomials
polymul.notes: Registry note 'n1*n2' is stale; code bills the FMA=2 convolution count 2*n1*n2 - n1 - n2 (n2 fixed at 100 here); min-clamped at 1.

polysub.describe: polysub of 1000*s-coeff and fixed 100-coeff all-ones polynomials
polysub.formula: max(n1, n2), n1/n2 = coefficient array lengths
polysub.notes: Same skeleton as polyadd: cost = max of the two lengths, data-independent; min-clamped at 1.

polyval.describe: degree-7 polynomial (8 coeffs) evaluated at 1000*s points
polyval.formula: 2*m*deg, deg = len(p)-1, m = numel(x) (Horner's method, FMA=2)
polyval.notes: Scales with numel(x); deg fixed at 7 so cost = 14*m; min-clamped at 1.

put.describe: scatter 1000*s values into a 2000*s ones array at flat indices 0..1000*s-1
put.notes: Cost = number of scatter writes (indices.size), mode-independent and independent of destination size; mutates a in place.

put_along_axis.describe: scatter one value per row into a (100*s, 64) array along axis 1 (argmax-style keepdims indices)
put_along_axis.formula: (numel(arr) / arr.shape[axis]) * indices.shape[axis]  (elements scattered; indices.size when axis=None; 0 for empty arr)
put_along_axis.notes: scatter of (numel/axis_len)*idx_axis_len elements; production weights put it in the data-movement free tier (weight 0.0), so billed cost is 0 despite the nonzero raw flop_cost

putmask.describe: in-place masked write into a 1000*s ones array, every 3rd element True, values same length as a
putmask.notes: Charges the full destination size (mask scan), independent of True count; mutates a in place.

quantile.formula: num_outputs * axis_dim (= numel(a) for a dense reduce; independent of the number of q values)
quantile.notes: Prior input failed only because q is a required arg; identical cost path to percentile (Tier-2 partition model), no len(q) scaling; complex input rejected by numpy (registry: illegal).

select.describe: 2 bool conditions + 2 float choices, all (1000*s,) -> output numel 1000*s
select.input_code:
def make(dt, s=1):
    n = 1000 * s
    c1 = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool); c1[: n // 2] = True
    c2 = ~c1
    x = np.ones(n, dtype=dt)
    y = np.full(n, 2, dtype=dt)
    condlist = [c1, c2]
    choicelist = [x, y]
    return lambda: fnp.select(condlist, choicelist, default=0)
select.formula: numel(output) (true broadcast size of the result)
select.notes: Raw cost = numel(output) regardless of number of conditions; packaged weight table applies gather tier x4 on top; billing dtype resolved from choicelist dtypes.

stats.expon.cdf.describe: 1000*s evaluation points evenly spaced in [-3, 3], dtype dt (negative half hits the where branch, cost is shape-only)
stats.expon.cdf.notes: Flat 22 FLOPs/elem composite (z: 2, exp(-z): 17, 1-exp: 1, where: 2; FMA=2), data-independent; floors at 1 elem for empty input; billing dtype always float64 (input coerced).

stats.expon.pdf.describe: 1000*s evaluation points evenly spaced in [-3, 3], dtype dt (negative half hits the where branch, cost is shape-only)
stats.expon.pdf.notes: Flat 22 FLOPs/elem composite (z=(x-loc)/scale: 2, exp(-z): 17, /scale: 1, where: 2; FMA=2), data-independent; floors at 1 elem for empty input; billing dtype always float64 (input coerced).

stats.expon.ppf.describe: 1000*s probabilities evenly spaced in [0.05, 0.95], dtype dt
stats.expon.ppf.notes: Flat 27 FLOPs/elem composite (loc-scale*log1p(-q): 19, three where/cmp/and edge selects: 8; FMA=2); floors at 1 elem for empty input; billing dtype always float64 (input coerced).

stats.laplace.cdf.describe: 1000*s evaluation points evenly spaced in [-3, 3], dtype dt (covers both sign branches; both exp branches are eager so cost is shape-only)
stats.laplace.cdf.notes: Flat 40 FLOPs/elem composite: TWO eager exp branches (2x16=32) + 8 arith/cmp/select, since where() evaluates both sides; data-independent; floors at 1 elem for empty input; billing dtype always float64.

stats.laplace.pdf.describe: 1000*s evaluation points evenly spaced in [-3, 3], dtype dt
stats.laplace.pdf.notes: Flat 22 FLOPs/elem composite (|x-loc|: 3, exp(-z): 17, /(2*scale): 2; FMA=2); floors at 1 elem for empty input; billing dtype always float64 (input coerced).

stats.laplace.ppf.describe: 1000*s probabilities evenly spaced in [0.05, 0.95], dtype dt (both log branches are eager so cost is shape-only)
stats.laplace.ppf.notes: Flat 51 FLOPs/elem composite: TWO eager log branches (2x16=32) + 19 arith/cmp/select incl. maximum clamps and 4 where edge selects; data-independent; floors at 1 elem for empty input; billing dtype always float64.

stats.logistic.cdf.describe: 1000*s evaluation points evenly spaced in [-3, 3], dtype dt
stats.logistic.cdf.notes: Flat 21 FLOPs/elem composite (z: 2, exp(-z): 17, 1+ez: 1, 1/denom: 1; FMA=2); floors at 1 elem for empty input; billing dtype always float64 (input coerced).

stats.logistic.pdf.describe: 1000*s evaluation points evenly spaced in [-3, 3], dtype dt
stats.logistic.pdf.notes: Flat 23 FLOPs/elem composite (z: 2, exp(-z): 17, 1+ez: 1, square: 1, scale*: 1, div: 1; FMA=2); floors at 1 elem for empty input; billing dtype always float64 (input coerced).

stats.logistic.ppf.notes: Flat 28 FLOPs/elem (logit: 1-q + q/(1-q) + log(16) + loc/scale affine(2) + 3 where(8)); value-independent; base coerces input to float64 so it always bills as float64; empty input floors at 1 elem.

stats.lognorm.cdf.notes: Flat 70 FLOPs/elem (log + erf rational approx + arithmetic); value-independent (support masking via where, all branches eager); shape param s=0.5 passed positionally; bills as float64 after internal coercion.

stats.lognorm.pdf.notes: Flat 62 FLOPs/elem (log + exp + arithmetic); value-independent; shape param s=0.5 passed positionally (avoids collision with scale kwarg name); bills as float64 after internal coercion.

stats.lognorm.ppf.notes: Flat 106 FLOPs/elem (ndtri rational approx + Newton polish + exp); value-independent; shape param 0.5 positional; bills as float64 after internal coercion.

stats.norm.cdf.notes: Flat 48 FLOPs/elem (erf rational approx + arithmetic); value-independent; bills as float64 (base coerces input); empty input floors at 1 elem.

stats.norm.pdf.notes: Flat 27 FLOPs/elem (exp + arithmetic composite); value-independent; bills as float64 (base coerces input); empty input floors at 1 elem.

stats.norm.ppf.notes: Flat 83 FLOPs/elem (Acklam rational ndtri + Newton polish with erf+exp); value-independent; bills as float64 (base coerces input).

stats.truncnorm.cdf.notes: Flat 51 FLOPs/elem (z(2) + std-normal-cdf erf composite(46) + result(3) + 2 where(4), scalar-bound Phi(a)/Phi(b) amortized into the per-elem constant); value-independent; bills as float64.

stats.truncnorm.pdf.notes: Flat 28 FLOPs/elem (z(2) + std-normal-pdf(20) + div(1) + bounds mask(5)); value-independent; scalar Phi(a)/Phi(b) normalizer amortized into constant; bills as float64.

stats.truncnorm.ppf.notes: Flat 81 FLOPs/elem (scalar erf CDFs at bounds + affine remap + ndtri rational approx per elem); value-independent; bills as float64 (base coerces input).

stats.uniform.cdf.notes: Flat 4 FLOPs/elem (sub + div + clip = 2 compare/selects); value-independent; input spans below/inside/above support to exercise both clip branches; bills as float64.

stats.uniform.pdf.describe: x = 1000s evenly spaced points on [-0.5, 1.5] (spans inside and outside the unit support), dtype dt; default loc=0, scale=1
stats.uniform.pdf.notes: Declared flat 1 FLOP/elem (_base.py: cost_per_elem*max(numel,1)); actual kernel does ~4 numpy ops/elem (2 compares + AND + where select) but code charges 1*numel; input cast to float64 internally so dtype-neutral billing; data-independent cost.

stats.uniform.ppf.describe: q = 1000s evenly spaced probabilities on [0, 1], dtype dt; default loc=0, scale=1
stats.uniform.ppf.notes: Declared flat 1 FLOP/elem (_base.py: cost_per_elem*max(numel,1)); actual kernel does ~6 numpy ops/elem (mul+add + 2 compares + AND + where NaN-mask) but code charges 1*numel; input cast to float64 internally so dtype-neutral billing; data-independent cost.

std.notes: Dense decomposition: 2 pointwise passes (center, square) = 2n, accumulation 2*(n-m), 2m divides, m sqrt; total is axis-independent except the +m sqrt term; ddof is cost-free; symmetric inputs are discounted to orbit counts by the reduction engine.

symmetrize.formula: (|G| + 1) * numel(data), |G| = symmetry-group order (|G| transposed-add passes + 1 scaling pass; min 1)
symmetrize.notes: Module flopscope (flops.symmetrize, not fnp). Cost is shape/group-only: (|G|+1)*numel with |G|=2 here => 3*numel; internal validation and transposes uncounted (decision D1); scales via the non-symmetric batch axis.

take.formula: numel(output) (gather: one index dereference per output element; output shape = indices shape)
take.notes: Cost set post-call from result.size (deduct_after); depends only on how many elements are gathered, not on source array size; scalar result charges 1.

take_along_axis.formula: numel(output) (gather: one index dereference per output element; output shape = broadcast(arr-minus-axis, indices))
take_along_axis.notes: Identical cost model to take (gather tier): raw cost = result.size via deduct_after; here output size == indices size = 1000s.

tensordot.formula: numel(output) * (2*K - 1), K = prod(contracted dims) (routed through the einsum (2K-1)*M contraction engine, FMA=2)
tensordot.notes: Cost = einsum accumulation total for the equivalent subscripts; symmetric operands scale cost by unique-element fraction and full-inner a-with-a contractions get joint-operand savings; complex billing exact via complex_factor_override; rank>52 falls back to a.size*b.size//K.

tile.notes: Cost set post-call from result.size (deduct_after), so it is exactly numel(output) for any reps shape; empty output charges 1.

trace.formula: min(shape[axis1], shape[axis2]) * batch, batch = numel / (shape[axis1]*shape[axis2]) (diagonal sum per matrix; 0 if ndim<2 or an axis is empty)
trace.notes: Top-level numpy trace (linalg.trace is a separate op); offset argument is ignored by the cost model (always charges full min(m,n) per matrix); square input so cost = n = 64s.

trapezoid.notes: Cost is 4*y.size regardless of whether x or dx is supplied (x-array diff not billed extra); complex_factor 2.0.

trapz.formula: 4 * numel(y) (identical cost model to trapezoid; deprecated alias)
trapz.notes: Deprecated numpy alias (max_numpy 2.4; raises UnsupportedFunctionError when numpy lacks np.trapz); emits numpy DeprecationWarning on 2.2 but measures fine; cost identical to trapezoid.

tril.formula: numel(output) (= numel(input); masked-select copy of the full matrix)
tril.notes: Cost set post-call from result.size; output shape equals input shape so k (diagonal offset) does not change the charge; warns if input carries a SymmetricTensor symmetry.

trim_zeros.formula: numel(input) (value scan for the nonzero boundary, same convention as nonzero/count_nonzero)
trim_zeros.notes: Charges full numel(input) up front regardless of how many zeros are actually trimmed (all-ones input trims nothing, still 1000s); complex_factor 2.0.

triu.formula: numel(output) (= numel(input); masked-select copy of the full matrix)
triu.notes: Same cost model as tril: result.size via deduct_after, independent of diagonal offset k.

union1d.notes: Size-only concat-sort cost (sort_cost(n+m), floor 1); overlap/duplicate structure irrelevant.

unique.notes: Sort-based, size-only cost; return_index/inverse/counts kwargs and duplicate structure do not change the charge.

unique_all.notes: Array-API sibling of unique; always flat (_unique_cost with axis=None), size-only sort cost.

unique_counts.notes: Array-API sibling of unique; always flat, size-only sort cost.

unique_inverse.notes: Array-API sibling of unique; always flat, size-only sort cost.

unique_values.notes: Array-API sibling of unique; always flat, size-only sort cost.

unpackbits.describe: (1000*s,) uint8 arange (mod 256), full flattened unpack -> 8000*s bits
unpackbits.formula: numel(output) = 8*numel(input) for full unpack (count=/axis= change output numel)
unpackbits.notes: Code charges numel(OUTPUT) via deduct_after set_cost(result.size) — registry note 'numel(input)' is stale; numpy requires uint8 input, other dtypes raise (correct).

unstack.describe: (10, 100*s) ones unstacked along axis 0 into 10 arrays
unstack.notes: Requires numpy>=2.1 (raises UnsupportedFunctionError below); cost independent of axis choice.

unwrap.notes: 11 counted one-FLOP passes over diff(p) charged against numel(input) (2 mask-select passes free); data-independent, floor 1.

vander.describe: Vandermonde matrix of 1000*s points with explicit N=64 columns
vander.formula: len(x)*(N-2), N defaults to len(x); min 1
vander.notes: Registry note says len(x)*(N-1) but code (_counting_ops.py:531) and its docstring bill max(n*(N-2), 1) — code wins; N fixed at 64 so only n scales.

var.formula: 4*n (n = numel(input); independent of axis and output size)
var.notes: Same skeleton as std without sqrt: 2n pointwise + 2*(n-m) accumulate + 2m divides = exactly 4n for any axis (the m terms cancel); ddof cost-free; verified 4N for axis=0/1 on (100,20).

vdot.formula: 2*n - 1, n = flattened numel (n mul + n-1 add, conjugating dot)
vdot.notes: Cost via einsum 'i,i->' accumulation on flattened inputs; complex billed exactly via complex_factor_override (8n-2 real FLOPs).

vecdot.formula: (2*n - 1) * b (n = contracted last-axis length, b = numel(output), i.e. batch size; unbatched 1-D case: 2*n - 1)
vecdot.notes: Einsum-routed ('...n,...n->...'): n multiplies + (n-1) adds per output dot; batched (7,50) verified at 7*(2*50-1)=693; complex billed exactly (complex_factor 'exact'); linalg.vecdot note's '2*n' is the rounded version of 2n-1. Requires numpy >= 2.1.

vecmat.formula: (2*n - 1) * numel(output) (n = contracted axis length; output is (..., m), so unbatched: m*(2*n - 1))
vecmat.notes: NEW input (old (1000,)+(1000,) fails: vecmat needs (n,)+(n,m)); scales the contracted dim n=64s with m=64 fixed; einsum-routed ('...n,...nm->...m') charges (2n-1)*outputs, so the registry note 'output_size * contracted_axis' (n*m) is stale; batched (5,30)x(5,30,8) verified at 5*8*59=2360. Requires numpy >= 2.2.

vstack.notes: Copy cost = total input elements (= output numel), floor 1; symmetry transport does not affect the charge.

where.describe: 1-arg form where(cond) on a 1-D all-ones array of length 1000*s (the charged nonzero-equivalent path)
where.notes: Two billing paths: 1-arg (== nonzero, derives indices by testing values) charges numel(condition) regardless of values; 3-arg mask-select is free (weight-0 deduct, time-accounted only) per the data-movement free-tier model. Canonical input exercises the charged 1-arg path; 3-arg path verified to bill 0 at both scales.
